# **2\. Funnel**

## **Critical Path**

Homepage Visit → Signup Started → Account Created → Athlete Profile Completed → Highlight Film Uploaded

| Funnel Step | Users | Conversion Rate |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Homepage Visit | 42 | 100% |
| Signup Started | 21 | 50% |
| Account Created | 13 | 62% |
| Athlete Profile Completed | 7 | 54% |
| Highlight Film Uploaded | 4 | 57% |

# **3\. Written Analysis**

Most traffic came from direct outreach through Columbia athletics connections, team group chats, and personal referrals. Users who already had active recruiting interest showed significantly stronger engagement compared to colder outreach traffic.

The largest drop-off occurs between account creation and completing the athlete profile. Thirteen users created accounts, but only seven completed onboarding and filled out their recruiting profile. Based on user testing sessions, the onboarding process currently asks for too much information too early, especially around statistics, achievements, and media uploads. Several users hesitated once they reached the profile setup stage and stopped before finishing the process.

Another noticeable drop-off occurs between profile completion and uploading highlight film. Some users did not immediately have highlight clips prepared or were unsure about what type of content should be uploaded. This created friction during the activation process.

To address these issues, onboarding is being simplified by reducing the number of required fields during initial signup and allowing users to access the platform before fully completing their profile. A progress bar and clearer onboarding instructions are also being added to make setup feel faster and more manageable. In addition, clearer examples of acceptable highlight film uploads will be added to reduce hesitation during the upload step.

Even with a relatively small sample size, the pattern is consistent across both analytics data and live user testing. Users who complete onboarding are significantly more likely to continue exploring the platform, while incomplete onboarding almost always leads to early drop-off.
